question: What the production screen's four build buttons do before a builder window shows, how the builders write the practical a unit gives, and two details of the division designer the first fragment passed over.

addresses.name: CProductionView::OnBuildDivision
addresses.comment: **The handler behind the production screen's `build_division_button`.** Hides every dialog the screen owns (CProductionView::HideDialogs), hides the screen's own window (+0xA8, slot 14 of its CGuiObject), shows its frame again (CProductionView::ShowFrame), shows the dialog at +0x300 - the division designer - through its slot 2, and tail-jumps to the view's own slot 5. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-builders.md, section 7.
addresses.evidence: `call 0x802260`; `mov ecx,[esi+0xa8]; mov eax,[ecx+0x18]; mov edx,[eax+0x38]; add ecx,0x18; call edx`; `call 0x801f80`; `mov ecx,[esi+0x300]; mov eax,[ecx]; mov edx,[eax+8]; call edx`; `mov edx,[eax+0x14]; jmp edx`. Stored as an observer's handler by the view's constructor at 0x7FB393.

addresses.name: CProductionView::ShowFrame
addresses.comment: **What is left of the production screen behind a builder window.** Shows eight elements of the screen's own window by name, each through its slot 13: the icons `bg_countryskin`, `bg_mainshadow` and `production_topitem`, the button `close_button`, the text `headline_prod`, the text `automation_setting`, and the buttons `mode_arrow_right` and `mode_arrow_left`. Called straight after the window is hidden, so hiding a window hides what is in it and these come back: the builders' own art is mostly transparent and is drawn to go over exactly this. `bg_prod`, the screen's background, is not among them. The name is ours.
addresses.evidence: The decompiled C: eight `std::string::assign` of the names, each followed by the window's slot 17, 13, 14 or 15 by the kind of element and slot 13 of what comes back. The art: 5.6% of production_divdesign_bg.dds is opaque.

addresses.name: CProductionView::HideDialogs
addresses.comment: Hides the seven dialogs the production screen owns - slot 3 of each of +0x300, +0x310, +0x314, +0x31C, +0x304, +0x308 and +0x30C, the last by tail jump - after hiding and deleting the one at +0x318 when there is one. The view in ESI. The name is ours.
addresses.evidence: The decompiled C: the test and the two virtual calls on `[esi+0x318]`, then seven `[...]+0xc` calls in that order.

addresses.name: FormatFixedPointTrimmed
addresses.comment: **A CFixedPoint as text with only the decimals it needs**: the whole part, then up to three decimal places with trailing noughts dropped, and no point at all for a whole number - `2`, `0.5`, `1.25`. A minus sign for a negative. `ret 8`. FormatFixedPoint (0x65ACA0) is its neighbour with a fixed number of places. The builder windows write `on_complete_impact` with it, after a `+`. The name is ours.
addresses.evidence: `imul` by 0x10624DD3 and `sar edx,6` for the whole part; the remainder plus 1000 printed in base ten so its first digit can be overwritten with `.` (`mov byte ptr [edi],0x2e`); `cmp byte ptr [edi+3],al` / `[edi+2]` / `[edi+1]` against `0` cutting the string at the first place that is not one; `ret 8` at 0xA5AC9B.

addresses.name: CDivisionDesigner::AddBrigade
addresses.no_signature: the receiver arrives in ESI and the type on the stack
addresses.comment: **Adds a unit type to the design if there is room.** The designer in ESI, the type on the stack. Room is `count (+0x1BC) < (BRIGADES_IN_DIVISION + CTechnologyStatus +0x1C) / 1000`. **The type is inserted by a CPrioComparator with its byte clear** (0x7EFB70), so the design is kept by its types' own `priority`, largest first, equals in the order they were added - and its first brigade, which a division is named for, is the one of the highest priority. Then RebuildBrigadeQueue and UpdateDesign. Called by CPossibleBrigadeEntry's click (0x7EFA40). Ghidra's RTTI pass had labelled this address a CPrioComparator constructor; it is not one. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-builders.md, section 2.
addresses.evidence: `mov eax,[esi+0x1bc]`; GetDefines, `[eax+0xac]` then `+0x80`, plus `[technology status + 0x1c]`, the divide by 1000 as a multiply by 0x10624DD3, and the compare; `mov byte ptr [esp+0x18],0; mov dword ptr [esp+0x14],0x15dd958; call 0x7efb70` (0x7EA8FF..0x7EA90C), 0x15DD958 being CPrioComparator's vftable; `call 0x7e4d60`, `call 0x7e6160`; `ret 4`.
addresses.revises: adds which comparator the insert uses, which the first reading had not looked at: the design is ordered by priority and not as clicked

addresses.name: CPossibleBrigadeEntry::CPossibleBrigadeEntry
addresses.no_signature: three stack arguments, `ret 0xC`, and a returned `this`; not typed
addresses.comment: **The constructor of one line of the brigade picker, which is where its columns are written.** A `brigade_entry_2` window. **Its `select` button takes the sprite `GFX_divdesigner_listbutton` + the type's unit_group as a number when a sprite of that name exists** - the line is coloured by its combined arms group. It makes a CRegiment of the type with every technology at the country's level, summing the levels, and from that definition writes `str` (max_strength * 100 through 0xAB7380), `org`, `cw`, `sa`, `ha`, `aa`, `piercing`, `armored`, `def`, `ad`, `tou`, `sup` and `off` with no decimals, `sof` as softness * 100 + `%`, `speed` through 0x5A54F0, `sc` and `fc` with two, `ic` as GetBuildCostIC(country, definition, levels, false) and `mp` as GetBuildCostManpower(country, definition, false) with two, and `time` as GetBuildTime(country, definition, levels) whole. CPossibleSingleBrigadeEntry's constructor (0x7DE3B0, `brigade_entry_3`) is the same length to the byte. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-builders.md, section 2.
addresses.evidence: `mov eax,[eax+0x1b4]`, `_itoa`, `'GFX_divdesigner_listbutton'` and `operatorPlus`, StringHashFind on the sprite table, then `'select'` and slot 57 (0x7EE5B6..0x7EE6EB). 0x7EEB7A..0x7EF948: each element's name pushed, then `mov ecx,[edi+N]` with N = 0xF0, 0xE8, 0x134, 0x138, 0x140, 0x13C, 0x12C, 0x11C, 0x128, 0x120, 0x130, 0x110, 0x114, 0x118 and `push 0` or `push 2` before `call 0xa5aca0`; `push 0x186a0` and the divide by 1000 on +0xEC and +0x124; `call 0x4e18f0`, `call 0x4e1880`, `call 0x4e19a0; ... call 0xa5ab40`.
addresses.revises: adds the sprite of the line's button, which the first reading passed over

frontier.why: CProductionView slot 5, which every build button's handler ends on

notes: The four handlers are observer targets and sit in no virtual table.
